proposal.description: The LATCH_ASSERT and OTP cause bits are laid out in swapped positions, so OTP is ranked above the CPLD's latch trip
proposal.reason: An OTP while running sets fault_reg bit 3 instead of bit 2, and a CPLD latch trip sets bit 2 instead of bit 3, so the host decodes each of these causes as the other.

proposal.description: The capture gate closes as soon as the protection latch reads back set, treating a set latch as a converter that has already stopped
proposal.reason: An analog OVP trip while running (latch_state high, latch_assert low) is never recorded in fault_reg bit 4. episode_start still fires, so fault_time keeps being re-latched while the record stays empty. Causes that arrive after a CPLD trip's readback follows are also dropped.

proposal.description: The OVP bit is recorded from the raw latch readback instead of the inferred ovp, so every CPLD-originated latch trip is also recorded as OVP
proposal.reason: After an overcurrent CPLD trip while running, once the SCR readback follows latch_assert, fault_reg shows OVP (bit 4) as well as LATCH_ASSERT (bit 3), even though no analog overvoltage happened.

proposal.description: OVP is recorded even while the converter is stopped, on the assumption that the analog comparator can trip the latch at any time and should always be logged
proposal.reason: If the latch is set by an analog trip and the converter is stopped, a host read does not leave the record empty: bit 4 is set again on the next clock. episode_start does not fire, so fault_time stays 0 next to a non-empty record.

proposal.description: Recording the LATCH_ASSERT (OCP/SCP) trip withdraws the OVERCURRENT bit, on the assumption that the latch bit already covers the window trips that led to it
proposal.reason: When window trips run up strikes until the CPLD asserts latch_assert while running, fault_reg ends up with only bit 3 set. The OVERCURRENT bit 0, recorded earlier, is lost, although bits are meant never to be cleared individually.
